parsed.main_gap: Both halves of the key refinement lemma are only sketched; the sweep/cancellation argument uses undefined objects ('arrays', 'column-blocks') and internally inconsistent quantitative claims, so neither bound is actually established.

errors.description: Proof of lemma (i) is unverifiable and internally inconsistent: it asserts the two post-cancellation arrays have totals summing to T-d yet each at most (T-d)/2 (forcing exact equality, which fails in examples), and that each has 'at most s column-blocks'. 'Arrays'/'column-blocks' are never defined, nor is it shown that cuts in these derived objects correspond to legal cuts of the actual pieces, so the induction cannot be checked.
errors.quote:
What remains, apart from the initial portion of length $d$, consists of two arrays, each with at most $s$ column-blocks and each of total length at most
\[
\frac{T-d}{2}=(2^s-1)d.
\]

errors.description: Proof of lemma (ii) (Liu's lower bound) asserts an inductive dichotomy about uncancelled d-strips versus a cut in every column, with no real justification of the inductive step; the phrase 'two identical copies of all preceding strips plus one parity interchange' is asserted rather than proved, and the counting 'requires at least s+1 cuts' is not derived.
errors.quote: Inductively, after the first $j+1$ columns have been swept, either one whole $d$-strip remains uncancelled in the odd row, or a cut has occurred in every one of these $j+1$ columns

errors.description: The write-up defers the 'full' proof of the central lemma to an external file not present in the submission, and the concluding cross-references are mislabelled (equations (5) and (6) are the integral formula and Liu's partition, not the two bounds (7) and (8)).
errors.quote: We use the following lemma, proved in full in `lemmas/refinement.md`.

parsed.notes: Correct final answer 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1), correct and rigorous reduction of the claiming phase to the alternating imbalance, correct extremal partition and correct lemma statements. The decisive combinatorial lemma, however, is only sketched, so the proof is not complete.
